rubricCompatibility.compatibilityScope: rule 10b audited 2026-11-13 on 20 countries (8 engineered-discovery, 6 visibility-sensitive, 6 random) plus 7 divisions, A/B against the same sample with the rule stripped: rule effect mean -0.004, mean |effect| 0.013, max 0.038, all below the prespecified thresholds of 0.03 mean and 0.08 max. A single-arm comparison had appeared to shift scores by +0.036, but an A/B control showed ~+0.039 of that came from partner resampling, not the rule.
rubricCompatibility.note: Scores keep their r2026-11-12 stamp. Compatibility with r2026-11-13 is supported within the audited sample, not proven for every record.

reproducibilityAudit.statusScope: reproducibilityAudit.status is the verifier's own verdict on this run and is independent of the consistency field, which covers only this builder's count/rubric/instrument reconciliation: a passing consistency field does not mean the audit passed.
reproducibilityAudit.withdrawnCaveat: An earlier 'incomplete provenance' class covering 73 records was WITHDRAWN after the production-log selection was corrected: those records reconcile exactly from redo_c4 alone, so the problem was my log selection, not missing data. Retained here as audit history rather than deleted.
reproducibilityAudit.basisAttribution: Attribution evidence for the production basis: the final rebalance ran with an explicit log list of redo_c4 only (commit e33802aa and successors), and recency_wave's writes are not reflected in any stored score.
reproducibilityAudit.productionBasis: countries from redo_c4 only, divisions from anchored_results. recency_wave is retained as history but was superseded: including it created 73 spurious gaps and it is required to reconcile no record.
reproducibilityAudit.claimBoundary: Agreement within the declared threshold is not complete historical provenance, and this manifest does not claim full reproduction: the current run reproduces 2304 of 3474 records exactly, 1169 within rounding level, 0 reconciling only within the 0.02 tolerance, and 1 outside it. A published value the archive does not reproduce is reported as a mismatch (see worstGapRows and output) and is never reinterpreted as an archived score
reproducibilityAudit.honestScope: Expected values are computed from archived logs without using any published score as an input; where a child feeds a parent the RECONSTRUCTED child value is used and dependency cycles are reported. Routing metadata (derivedFrom.mode, inherited, estimated, the no-signal template) is read from the publication and is therefore taken as given, not independently derived — a disclosed limitation. Published-and-published consistency also holds but is not counted as provenance.
reproducibilityAudit.toleranceJustification: 0.02 is the pipeline's own declared settlement precision, reported alongside exact matches so a reader can see the difference between faithful reproduction and agreement within the declared threshold.

logArchive.note: gzipped JSONL of the rating runs whose means the published scores were computed from; enough to recompute every stored score derived from archived ratings, with intentional overrides recorded in reproducibilityAudit rather than reproduced from these logs

productionProvenance.comparabilityWarning: Scores are outputs of a measurement procedure at a point in time, not timeless measurements. Differences of a few hundredths between versions should not be read as substantive country change without a sentinel replay; research/experiments/2026-11-13-replay-sentinel.json records the current sentinel panel and its spread.

notes.inherited: Divisions with no sub-national signal take the national score and are NOT independent evidence; they are excluded from any aggregation over divisions.
notes.instruments: Countries with measured divisions are not all means: 133 of 174 publish a destination summary (mean of their divisions) with nationalFrameworkScore kept as supplementary context, 21 publish their nationalFrameworkScore as their score (the staged national-assessment rollout and countries whose provenance records no destination summary because of endpoint-clamping), 19 publish a framework rating with no nationalFrameworkScore field (provenance: no measured division set), and a provisional override covers the remaining 1: a country-level score that is neither its divisions' mean nor its own nationalFrameworkScore (see reproducibilityAudit). Divisions are calibrated to the frozen anchor version recorded here.
notes.anchorDrift: The anchors' displayed country scores have moved since the division pass (national re-aggregation). The pass is versioned to the frozen constants, not to today's country scores; a replacement ladder requires independent validation.
